newsitem.title: POLAND: Denmark's Rasmussen lends support to Polish goals.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Rasmussen lends support to Polish goals.

text.p: Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen pledged Danish support for Warsaw's NATO and EU aspirations on Tuesday, proclaiming that Danes were the most avid foreign investors in Poland.

"I am very proud to state that Denmark is investing the most, per capita, among all foreigners who invest in Poland," Rasmussen told a news conference in Warsaw after talks with President Aleksander Kwasniewski.

Rasmussen said he had told Kwasniewski he expected Poland to be among the first countries invited, at NATO's Madrid summit in July, to start talks on entering the alliance -- voicing a general assumption that Poland will be a front-runner.

He added that he hoped Warsaw's negotiations on European Union entry would be good and dynamic, while commenting that the adaptation of Poland's farming to European standards would have to be gradual, to protect Polish agricultural development.

On Monday, the start of his three-day visit, Rasmussen and his Polish counterpart Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz signed an agreement on grant aid from Denmark's government to Poland, to help its economic reforms and EU bid.

Rasmussen also stressed the importance of Baltic regional co-operation, proposing that Poland and Denmark launch a study into possible construction of a regional gas pipeline network, for future consideration by other countries around the sea.
This long-term project was welcomed in Poland, which will rely on Russian gas for decades and would like greater diversity of sources but can now only import small amounts from Norway by ship.
Cimoszewicz applauded the gas network idea on Tuesday, saying it built on an existing suggestion among Baltic countries for a shared electric power network.
"Poland would be very interested, as we would also like to buy Norwegian gas but there is now no means of delivery," he told public radio.
Denmark is the 12th largest investor in Poland, with equity and loans of $238 million invested so far, according to a January report by the Polish Agency for Foreign Investment.
Rasmussen is being accompanied on the trip by executives of around 40 Danish companies seeking business.
